definition: Noisy Embedding Instruction Fine Tuning, an algorithm which suggests adding noise to the embedding layer during forward pass of fine tuning.
details: Noisy Embedding Instruction Fine Tuning, an algorithm which suggests adding noise to the embedding layer during forward pass of fine tuning.

explainer.lead: NEFTune is a cheap fine-tuning tweak that adds noise to token embeddings during the forward pass. It can improve instruction-following quality without changing the model architecture.

tiers.eli5: It's like practising a speech with a little background noise, so you learn to cope with messy input instead of only perfect conditions.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it by injecting random noise into the embedding layer only during fine-tuning forward passes; a common pitfall is forgetting that the noise is training-only and must be off at inference.
tiers.paperLevel: During the forward pass of fine-tuning, random noise is added to the embedding vectors; the definition specifies no noise scale or schedule, so its magnitude must be chosen empirically.

explainer.example: A team fine-tuning an instruction model adds noise to each token embedding while training, then disables it for deployment.
